name: Ají de Gallina (Peruvian Creamy Yellow Pepper Chicken)
why: One of Peru's greatest comfort foods and a brilliant technique lesson: the sauce gets its body from a bread-and-walnut purée plus evaporated milk and Parmesan — no cream at all — while aji amarillo brings a fruity golden heat. It's the perfect hands-off Sunday: poach, blend, simmer, done.
ingredients: 2 cups chicken stock (more as needed to cover chicken)
1-2 tbsp aji amarillo paste (start with 1, add to taste)
For serving: hard-boiled eggs, pitted black olives, boiled yellow potatoes, steamed rice

steps: In a large zip bag, combine chicken thighs with salt, garlic powder, onion powder and 2 tsp aji amarillo paste. Coat thoroughly and refrigerate 4 hours, up to overnight.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, add the marinated thighs and 2 cups chicken stock (enough to just cover). Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce to a simmer.
Poach until cooked through (internal temp ~74°C), about 15-20 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate to rest; reserve the cooking liquid — the sauce depends on it.
In a bowl, combine the bread, walnuts and 1/2 cup reserved stock. Let the bread soak, then blitz in a blender until completely smooth.
In the same Dutch oven, heat oil over medium. Cook onion and garlic until translucent, about 5 minutes.

Stir in the bread-walnut purée, turmeric, 1 tbsp aji amarillo paste, salt and cumin, then 1 cup reserved stock. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer and cook 15 minutes. Taste and add more aji amarillo paste to your heat level.
Start boiling water for the potatoes and get the rice going — the sauce keeps while they cook.
Shred the chicken with two forks and return it to the pot.
Stir in the evaporated milk and Parmesan until melted and glossy. Thin with more reserved stock if the sauce is too thick. Simmer 5 more minutes, tasting for seasoning.
Serve over steamed rice with boiled potatoes, hard-boiled eggs and black olives on the side.

pro_tips: No aji amarillo paste available? Use a mild yellow chili paste or even a pinch of turmeric + a dash of mild chilli sauce, but the fruity depth is what makes this dish sing — worth hunting down at a Latin grocery.
The bread-and-walnut purée is the secret thickener — don't skip the walnuts. For extra richness, swap some of the evaporated milk for full-cream and add a knob of butter at the end.
author: Henry
